transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Evan Brooks, Priya Nair, Zoe Kim - Redwood; Liam O'Connor, Jasmine Wu, Diego Alvarez, Meera Patel - Clearpath Labs

Auto-summary (auto): Initial procurement/technical intake; focus on legal redlines, KMS, and pilot costing.

00:00:07 Evan Brooks: hey everyone thanks for carving out time today, we wanted to make sure we align on legal asks and the pilot timeline before we drop the pilot order in, quickly run through agenda - MSA/DPA redlines, sla/latency targets, kms and keying, and then the pilot sizing.
00:00:36 Liam O'Connor: yep that sounds good, we have a short procurement window, target to sign pilot by end of october, so hoping we can close the legal path quick.
00:00:50 Jasmine Wu: from legal's side quick note - we have three non negotiables: data residency terms for EU data, indemnity cap language, and audit log retention for 7 years. we'll flag exact sections after this call.
00:01:12 Priya Nair: understood, thanks jasmine; on the kms side we support Redwood-managed keys, customer-managed keys in KMS, and HSM integrations - curious which variant is preferred?
00:01:29 Diego Alvarez: we prefer customer-managed KMS, ideally rotation controlled by our security team; also want E2E encryption for at-rest and in-transit and an audit trail.
00:01:45 Zoe Kim: that's doable - for Private deployments we can integrate your KMS; for Dedicated we also offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for certain regions. I'll note that we need to flush out key rotation windows and role-based access.
00:02:10 Meera Patel: timeline question - if we sign pilot by Oct 31, when can we expect a live pilot? two weeks? four weeks?
00:02:25 Evan Brooks: pilot slotted for 2-3 weeks to go live after legal and infra okays; realistically 3 weeks to allow for onboarding, test suite and a small-scale load test.
00:02:40 Liam O'Connor: ok that maps to our timeline, procurement needs a clear SLA and fallback if the dedicated nodes aren't stable.
00:03:05 Priya Nair: about SLA - we propose a pilot SLA that's more lenient: 99.5% for pilot window, with production GA SLA options of 99.95% for Dedicated and 99.9% for Hosted plus an escalation path. Important to set error budget and rollback policies in the SLO.
00:03:32 Jasmine Wu: what's the penalty structure if SLA is missed? legal will want measurable credits or a remediation plan.
00:03:46 Evan Brooks: standard approach is service credits scaled to downtime; we can include a structured credit schedule in the SOW - i'll surface the example in the template.
00:04:05 Diego Alvarez: and if there is a regional outage, do we have automatic fallback to another region or to hosted? what's the network egress impact?
00:04:16 Priya Nair: we support smart routing - there's an automated fallback policy that can route to Hosted in a different region or to a compatible model variant. Egress billing can increase if you cross region, and that's something to estimate - we'll share an egress cost model.
00:04:37 Liam O'Connor: for procurement, we need upfront visibility on egress fees - last vendor surprised us with outbound network fees during tests.
00:04:49 Zoe Kim: totally — we can add a sample cost calc showing token volumes, typical egress payload sizes, and caching assumptions; note that prefix/K-V caching can reduce egress and token cost but might change security posture.
00:05:18 Meera Patel: quick clarification - you said prefix KV cache, what's that mean?
00:05:24 Priya Nair: sorry bad speak, KV cache - key-value cache for transformer attention caches; it keeps recent conversation context server-side to lower compute per token. sometimes the transcript says K-V cash — not cash — kash, lol.
00:05:42 Jasmine Wu: ha, noted, we just need it documented because caching affects retention of conversation fragments and could be a compliance question.
00:05:58 Evan Brooks: on MSA redlines - we typically accept standard procurement clauses, but customer-specific indemnity caps and security carve-outs will be flagged. to speed things up, i'll send our template + a redline-friendly version indicating typical concessions.
00:06:18 Liam O'Connor: great. in terms of procurement path we have two committees: legal + security review, then a final procurement signoff. the security review requires penetration test report and SOC2 attestation. do you provide SOC2 type II?
00:06:36 Zoe Kim: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs; i'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.
00:06:48 Diego Alvarez: penetration tests - do you support a customer-run pentest against Dedicated? some vendors limit that.
00:06:57 Priya Nair: we allow customer pentests in Dedicated with a pre-approved test scope and windows; for Hosted we have a shared pen test program.
00:07:14 Jasmine Wu: what about audit logs retention? we said 7 years, some vendors only store 1 year; is 7 years feasible?
00:07:26 Evan Brooks: seven years is above our standard retention; we'll need to coordinate with engineering - might be an add-on. i'll flag that as an item when i circulate the MSA notes.
00:07:42 Meera Patel: cost question - if we go Dedicated pilot 4 GPUs, what's the rough monthly? ballpark is fine for procurement planning.
00:07:54 Priya Nair: ballpark: depends on instance family and model. for a 4-GPU Dedicated pool on say A100 class, rough blended cost might be $25k-40k per month, but with pilot discounts and usage smoothing we can provide a 3-tier estimate. i'll send a spreadsheet.
00:08:18 Liam O'Connor: okay that helps, procurement will want unit economics per 1M tokens as well.
00:08:27 Zoe Kim: we'll provide per-token and per-embedding cost lines, and show how caching/quantization reduces unit cost.
00:08:40 Diego Alvarez: on KMS and keying: if we use customer KMS, do you still have access to plaintext logs for debugging? that's a security no-no for us.
00:08:53 Priya Nair: with BYOK, Redwood does not hold key material, so we can't decrypt customer data; we provide deterministic observability with redacted logs for debugging and optional secure debugging sessions where customer can grant time-limited access.
00:09:15 Jasmine Wu: that time-limited access must be logged and auditable.
00:09:20 Evan Brooks: noted, we'll capture that in the SOW and audit logging section.
00:09:32 Meera Patel: pilot acceptance criteria - what does success look like? latency thresholds, error rates, and inference accuracy on our test prompts?
00:09:43 Priya Nair: yes pilot success: p95 latency within agreed bound (e.g., 200-300ms per token for streaming, or we can set model-specific bounds), error rate under X% (we'll pick a number), and baseline QA on a canonical prompt set - we can add automatic evaluation harness.
00:10:10 Liam O'Connor: who signs off on acceptance internally? procurement or product?
00:10:18 Meera Patel: product + SRE signoff, legal signs off separately for contract.
00:10:25 Jasmine Wu: timeline again - we'd like to see the redline by Oct 7 so legal can review, otherwise we may need another week.
00:10:34 Evan Brooks: i'll get that out by Oct 7.
00:10:40 Zoe Kim: and i'll attach SOC2 and our pentest preconditions.
00:10:46 Diego Alvarez: for the cost model can you show a sensitivity table if latency target tightens? sometimes cost jumps nonlinearly when you force lower tail latency.
00:10:58 Priya Nair: yes, we can show tradeoffs: higher batch sizes reduce cost but increase latency, more replicas reduce tail latency but increase fixed cost. we'll include a sensitivity tab.
00:11:20 Liam O'Connor: any blockers from Redwood for our BYOK request?
00:11:26 Priya Nair: no blockers in principle; we need key rotation policy, KMS provider details, and to map who will hold IAM roles.
00:11:38 Meera Patel: will we get a sandbox account to pre-test integration?
00:11:43 Evan Brooks: yes we can provision a sandbox in Hosted to run basic integration tests while the Dedicated pilot is being provisioned.
00:11:55 Jasmine Wu: about data residency: we have EU customers; can you guarantee data stays in EEA for storage and processing for those customers?
00:12:06 Zoe Kim: for Private and Dedicated you can pin region; for Hosted we have region options and data processing agreements, but we'll need to scope region-specific routing.
00:12:20 Diego Alvarez: final note on monitoring: we need tokens-level tracing and the ability to redact PII in traces.
00:12:30 Priya Nair: we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns, sampling traces and PII redaction hooks; we'll document how to configure sampling.
00:12:45 Evan Brooks: okay great, let's recap next steps.
00:12:49 Evan Brooks: Evan to send MSA/DPA redlines by Oct 7, Priya to send Dedicated config and cost estimate by Oct 9, Zoe to share SOC2 + pen-test guidelines today, Jasmine to send legal must-haves by Oct 10, Diego to share egress baseline by Oct 10. we'll tentatively schedule a follow up for Oct 13 to review redlines and cost.
00:13:20 Liam O'Connor: sounds good thanks everyone.
00:13:24 Meeting end (recording stopped).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (KV/cache rendered as K-V cash), speaker attribution may be approximate; timestamps are approximate.
